lines.en: : Shi-chan! Hi. Status report, please. How goes the hunt for my half-sister? Or whatever it is I’m supposed to call her if she wasn’t actually created by my dad.
: You know, you should really get a DNA test. I know you’re suspicious too and that’s one of the few answers I’m of virtually no help with.
: The status report is that I’m going to need you to cover my next three shifts to make up for what I’m going through right now.
: That tough to find, huh?
: No, I found her alright. I was just unaware of how much of a mess she was going to make.
: Oh, you did?! But, wait. A mess as in-
: As in the same thing you called me to clean up at the dorms. Just this time, I have to tend to a flower garden as well. So thanks for that. I hate flowers.
: But I’m a flower and you love me.
: Five shifts now. I’m serious, Himawari. This is a much bigger job than I expected.
: Thankfully, there were five grouped up here at Tsukioka Manor. Seems like your “half-sister” had a post-apocalyptic craving for arts and crafts and decided to saw some rich girls into pieces.
: Think she caught on that we were here, though. Hung herself from a tree before I even arrived and two of the girls still have all of their parts attached. Left a note too.
: Also, she can’t fly, can she?
: What? Obviously not.
: Guess she’s just very good at climbing trees then. I’m going to need to go back for a ladder or I won’t be able to get her down.
: I need some more boxes anyway, though, so I guess it’s not that big of a deal.
: Who does that leave then? If there are five, does that mean Nodoka’s there? Or are some of dad’s older friends still unaccounted for?
: I think that’s everyone. Plus one extra since there were two of that Fukuyama girl for some reason.
: Yeah, that happens here sometimes. Think there’s some sort of glitch causing certain girls to replicate during the pause.
: Dad said she was acting strangely earlier, so that might have something to do with why she-
: I don’t care. This place sucks and I don’t want to help with it anymore. Just let this world collapse and smuggle your parents back to your dream world so you can all disappear together.
: I’m really sorry, Shi-chan. I just didn’t have anybody else to ask for help. All the other reps who are already familiar with this terminal have it out for me.
: I wonder if that has anything to do with how you’re constantly shaking their ant farm.
: That probably has something to do with it, yeah.
: To be honest, I’m surprised this one has lasted this long in the first place. I’d have condemned it from the get-go if I was the one in charge.
: You say that about every world you visit.
: Sure, but no one from any of those worlds has known about us. If this Ami girl were to escape somehow and took that information with her, she’d be putting everything at risk.
: I know. I completely agree. But nothing has worked so far so, like...what can we even do about it?
: File an F4972-B. We need to bring in a Peerless One if nothing we do is working. She’s too big of a risk.
: None of them will touch her. Those forms always come back rejected.
: Rejected? No, that can’t be right.
: It is, though. I can show you the next time we go to the office.
: Himawari, the only time those forms are rejected is if the party in question is already under the protection of a god. And Ami doesn’t have a contract with anyone. At least not a legal one.
: Can’t be a snake oil deal either. They register their clients even faster than we do so they don’t keep getting solicited and pressured into better partnerships.
: You’re the expert here, Shiori-Senpai. I don’t know most of that official stuff yet. I just know what I’ve seen.
: Ugh...god damn it. Now I’m curious and I have to look into it. I can’t believe you roped me into this bullshit.
: Should have just given your dad a mop. Let him be scarred for all I care. I feel like an actual janitor today with how much blood I’ve had to clean off of everything.
: Again, I’m sorry. You were my last hope and I’ll do whatever I can to make it up to you.
: But if that’s everything and there’s no one left to be found, is it okay if I-
: Yeah. Go enjoy your final hours in whatever the hell this place is called. I’ll file the report once I finish up with these bodies.
: You can’t come back though, Himawari. Doing this through me is only going to make the target on your back bigger once the documents are reviewed.
: And what’s even better is that I’ll have one on my back now too. So that’s fun. I love being watched.
: Shi-chan-
: For the last time, stop calling me that or I will report you myself.
: Hah...
: That girl’s going to wind up like you one day, mysterious dead teenager who is hopefully named Nodoka. Just with much less fanfare and little to no artistic value.
: Now, let’s work on your memories.
: Assuming that Ami girl didn’t do anything to your face, that is. I’ve done enough reconstruction for one day. I hope you’re easy.
: Anyway, let’s see what I’m working with this time.
: Kyoko?...
: Great news, guys! Every cast member has now been accounted for and we are free to enjoy the rest of our time together like the world is not currently engrossed in a weird intermission!
: I take it your friend found Ami then? How was she? Was she still...sentient? Like you thought she’d be?
: Out like a light, so no questions this time. Same way Sana was. Shiori-Senpai’s taking care of her memory stuff now.
: How...was Sana exactly? I still don’t really understand what’s happening here...
: Just limp and lifeless basically, but not actually dead. Himawari says she’ll go back to normal once the world starts back up.
: People kind of just plop over once the “apocalypse” happens. Then I go around touching them until everyone is fixed. The end. That’s the condensed version of my job.
: I wish I could have seen you in action. But I also think that might make me sad since I did ultimately resign myself to you being an unemployed, stay-at-home daughter forever.
: Well, thats great news too! Because I really only took this job in the first place to try and make things better for you guys.
: I’m quitting as soon as I can get you out of here and starting up my own company instead. One that’ll really make the world a better place.
: Are things not...good for us in...whatever your main world is then?
: Sorry. That’s classified.
: Is this company you’re apparently going to start up classified as well?
: Depends. Are you going to use the information I give you to start up your own competing company before I am born and send my fate spiraling into an infinite pit of purposelessness?
: Do I look like the type of person who’d be able to run his own business, Himawari?
: You bastard. You’re already calling it your business when you know for a fact that it’s my idea. Hope you’re ready for a hefty lawsuit, buddy.
: Can you tell me, Hima-chan? If I promise not to compete against you?
: I don’t mind telling either of you guys, really. Or anyone for that matter. Because it’s less about the money and more about the possibility to me.
: If someone wants to do it first, that’s fine. But it’s something I want, so it’s something I will make if I really have to.
: The idea is simple — what if everyone got to have a happy ending?
: And what if there was some brilliant, blue-eyed angel out there who came up with a system in which that dream could become a reality?
: What if those worlds we wished for and perfect outcomes weren’t just temporary reprieves from collapsing timelines, but destinations one could visit any time they want to?
: Whether it be for a day, a week, or the rest of your life — the vision I have is one where everyone can do what I do. Go places I can and see all there is to see.

: The world we have now is unfair. The whole system is unfair — where wishes are granted for a you that isn’t you while a you who isn’t you gets to reap the benefits of it without doing any of the legwork.
: So I want to change that. I don’t want people to be stuck somewhere they aren’t happy. I want them to be free.
: And if they’re to be free, they shouldn’t be boxed in by worlds with walls on every side just because that’s where they woke up one day. You know what I mean?
: I do.
: Are you sure you don’t want to just open a boba shop instead, though? That sounds way easier and way more plausible.
: Oh, yeah. I guess boba makes people happy too. That does sound easier.
: So Hima-chan finally has a dream and you immediately shoot it down? Not even going to pretend it doesn’t sound completely insane?
: You think I don’t know it’s insane? Simply pitching that to somebody could earn me the ire of some spiteful god. Plus, I’m learning firsthand right now just how hard it is to do what I want to do.
: You guys are basically my first customers as an intergalactic tour guide. And I don’t think I need to tell you I’m doing a pretty terrible job after the Aomori fiasco.
: But I’m going to get better. And I might not be a god myself, but I don’t think they’re much stronger than humans in the grand scheme of things since we all feed off of each other.
: That said, who’s to say that anything really is impossible? Who’s to say that I can’t sculpt the universe myself when I’ve already made one?
: How though? Because if your weird, divine megacorp can’t manage to keep everything under control with both humans and gods on their side, how do you expect to?
: No clue. That boba idea is really starting to sound a lot more enticing, not gonna lie.
: Who’s stealing whose idea now?
: Oh, you slick son of a mother.
: Hima-chan, can I say something?
: Don’t ask me for permission. You’re my mom. Even if you’re the same age and only an inch or two taller right now.
: I just want to say that if anyone can make something like that happen, it’s you. You’ve already accomplished so much.
: Well, thank you...but, I really haven’t.
: Everything I’ve done so far has only made things worse. And if you guys can’t figure the rest out on your own, I...
: Everything will have been for nothing.
: No it won’t, Himawari.
: I mean it, though. If this world really does end-
: I don’t care what you mean. You’ve showed me that there’s more to life. That I can be happy. And that’s not something I’ve ever really believed before.
: I don’t know if it will happen in this world. Or whatever one I wind up in if we do get out of here.
: But it will happen somewhere. And I can take solace in just knowing that I’m doing better off somewhere else.
: And that one day, I will be the most average father to the most amazing daughter who has ever lived.
: You’ll have all the free boba you could ever imagine too. Promise.
: Hah...I hate that I cried for so long. I missed out on so much.
: Hima-chan, how much time do we have left? When do you need to leave?
: Soon, but...
: If it’s okay...
: I have an idea of where we can go next.
